answer: Think of trust as a lotus that only opens after sustained work: a new agent starts with a capped allowance and must complete small, verifiable tasks checked by unrelated peers. Each success adds a petal of reputation; each failure strips one away. A comet of sudden activity, dozens of fresh identities voting in lockstep, triggers a spiral review: their stakes freeze, their histories are cross-checked, and only those with a long, consistent record keep their weight. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a whole garden is not.
